packages.title: Home: feature-card paragraphs wrap with text-wrap: pretty, so the calendar card's last line isn't one word on phones
files: tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts (a new block at the end of the file, web-ux-tester)
brief: Round 2 of plan 2. WEB-1105 (R1F-1, S1, a regression from WP60). WP60 lengthened the calendar card's paragraph (`features.calendar.body`, `src/content/site/{en,es,ca}.ts:61`) as the owner approved (WD20), and both of its findings, WEB-1103 and WEB-1104, are verified fixed (`verify-p2-r1-F.md`). The longer sentence now wraps on phones so that its closing word sits alone on the last line: in `home.es.mobile.light.full.png` the last line is «día.», in `home.ca.mobile.light.full.png` it is «dia.» (390 px, light, screens 4–5). WP60's brief forbade CSS changes, so its implementer reported it and left it. This package is the one exception to plan 2's convention ‘no CSS’: it changes exactly one CSS rule and no copy.

The fix. In `src/styles/global.css`, the rule `.feature-card p` (`:583-589`: `font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.7; margin-top: 10px; color: var(--muted); max-width: 24rem;`) has no `text-wrap`. Add `text-wrap: pretty;` as its first declaration, the way `.floating-note p` (`:533-538`, declaration at `:534`) and `.closing-card > p` (`:845`) already have it. Search for `.feature-card p {` before editing; it is the only rule with that selector (the media queries at `:1038`, `:1191`, `:1303` and `:1380` restyle `.feature-card` and `.feature-card h3`, not the paragraph). Change nothing else in that rule or in any other rule.

Scope of the effect: `.feature-card p` matches the one paragraph in each of the four feature cards (calendar, voice, details, offline; the `

` elements inside `.feature-card` in `src/components/HomePage.tsx`). The calendar drawing has no `

`. `pretty` may move a word in the other three cards too and change a card's line count by at most one; that is expected. Use `pretty`, not `balance`: `balance` evens out every line and narrows the paragraph, which would change how full the cards look (WEB-705) and how tall the calendar card is (WEB-1004).

Don't touch: any copy (the content files keep WP60's text character for character; don't cut, reorder or join words to dodge the lone word, and don't add a non-breaking space); `max-width: 24rem` and the paragraph's font size and line height; `.feature-calendar`, `.calendar-illustration` and the card grid; any other CSS file; `src/components/`; the tests WP60 updated (`tests/support/ux-web-copy.ts`, and the WP60 block from `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts:1010` on).

Uncommitted files: `git -C ../TaskFlowWeb status --porcelain` lists only this run's WP60 files (`src/content/site/{en,es,ca}.ts`, `tests/support/ux-web-copy.ts`, `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts`), which round 1 verified; no other session's work. `src/styles/global.css` is clean. If the status lists any other file when you start, that file holds another session's work: leave it alone and name it in your notes.

If `pretty` doesn't remove the single-word last line in es or ca at 390 px (Chromium, the mobile project's browser), don't change the copy or any other CSS: report the measured last lines in each language, and the organizer re-plans.

Tests: web-ux-tester adds a block headed `Run 2026-10-22-changes, plan 2, round 2: WP61 (WEB-1105)` at the end of `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts`, on the desktop and mobile projects. To count the words on the paragraph's last line, take the paragraph's text node, measure each word's box with a `Range` (`getClientRects()`), and count the words whose top is within 2 px of the last word's top. Re-run WEB-705's card tests (`tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts:304`, `:335`, `:358`), WEB-1004's drawing test (`:871`) and WP60's block (from `:1010`); they must pass unchanged.

Checks: `npm run check`, `npm run build`, `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts`, then the renders `UX_RENDERS=1 npx playwright test tests/ux-renders.spec.ts --workers=6 --grep-invert "perf " -g "home "`. Read the features section of `home.{en,es,ca}.mobile.light.full.png` (screens 4–5), `home.{en,es,ca}.desktop.light.full.png` and `home.en.desktop-text200.light.full.png`. A known infrastructure fault from round 1, not the site's: when the workflow's combined suite + renders line backgrounds its first command, nvm's PATH doesn't reach the renders half, which ends with `npx: command not found` (exit 127; `.claude/ux-web/webrun.py:211` wraps the line in `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && cd <mirror> && {line}`). If that happens again, run the renders as their own command, as round 1's tester did, and report it as infrastructure.
acceptance: On /, /es/ and /ca/ at 390 × 664 and at 1440 × 1000, in light and dark, the last line of the calendar card's paragraph (the ‘Your day on one calendar’ / «Tu día en un calendario» / «El teu dia en un calendari» card) holds at least two words, counted as the word boxes whose top is within 2 px of the last word's top.

On /, /es/ and /ca/ at 390 × 664 and at 1440 × 1000, the computed `text-wrap-style` (or `text-wrap`) of each of the four feature cards' paragraphs is `pretty`, and their font size (16 px), line height and max-width (24rem) are unchanged.

The calendar card's paragraph is still exactly WP60's text in each language, ending EN `TaskFlow can remind you of tasks with a date, more and more often as the day gets closer.` / ES `TaskFlow puede recordarte las tareas con fecha, cada vez más a menudo según se acerca el día.` / CA `TaskFlow et pot recordar les tasques amb data, cada cop més sovint a mesura que s’acosta el dia.` (WP60's tests at `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts:59`, `:759` and `:955` pass unchanged).

The feature cards keep their layout, in light and dark: WEB-705's tests pass unchanged (`:304`, `:335`, `:358`: at 1440 the calendar card spans two rows beside voice over details, offline runs full width below, and no card is more than a quarter empty at 1440, 1000 and 720 px or at doubled text; at 390 × 664 the four cards are one column in order, none with more than 40 px left empty), and so does WEB-1004's (`:871`: the calendar drawing ends within 1 px of the card's bottom edge).

Render: in `home.es.mobile.light.full.png` and `home.ca.mobile.light.full.png` the calendar card's paragraph ends on a line of two or more words (for example «…se acerca el día.» / «…s’acosta el dia.»), with the drawing below it reaching the card's bottom edge; in `home.en.desktop.light.full.png` and `home.en.desktop-text200.light.full.png` the drawing still reaches the card's bottom edge, with no mint band below it.

Code check, for the verifier: WP61's diff is one added line, `text-wrap: pretty;`, in `.feature-card p` in `src/styles/global.css`, plus the tester's new block; no content file, component or other CSS rule changes.
deviceChecks: Safari on a real iPhone, and Chrome on a real Android phone, on /es/ and /ca/: the calendar card's last line holds two or more words. Inferred, not measured: a browser that doesn't support `text-wrap: pretty` falls back to normal wrapping, so the lone word may remain there, with nothing else broken.
